Name: 1-Chloronaphthalene
Desc: 1-chloronaphthalene is a clear colorless to amber oily viscous liquid.

Name: 1-Methyl Naphthalene
Desc: 1-methylnaphthalene is a colorless liquid. Freezing point -22°C (7.6°F). Boiling point 240-243°C (464-469°F). Flash point 82°C (180°F). Denser than water. Derived from coal tar and used in organic synthesis.

Name: 1-Methyl-4-(1-Methylethenyl)Benzene
Desc: P-Mentha-1,3,5,8-tetraene is a monocyclic hydrocarbon and a monoterpene.

Name: 1-Pentanol
Desc: Pentan-1-ol is an alkyl alcohol that is pentane in which a hydrogen of one of the methyl groups is substituted by a hydroxy group. It has been isolated from Melicope ptelefolia. It has a role as a plant metabolite. It is an alkyl alcohol, a primary alcohol, a pentanol and a short-chain primary fatty alcohol.

Name: 1-Pentylcyclopentane
Desc: A clear colorless to yellow viscous liquid used recently as an additive for organic solar cells and as as heat transfer fluids for High Temperature Energy Applications

Name: 1-Phenylnaphthalene
Desc: Clear liquid used in the manufacture of synthetic resins and rubber adhesives and also as a blowing agent in the manufacture of polyurethane insulating foam

Name: 1,2-Dimethoxybenzene (Veratrol)
Desc: 1,2-Dimethoxybenzene is a natural product found in Ophrys sphegodes, Averrhoa carambola, and other organisms with data available.

Name: 1,4-Cineole
Desc: 1,4-cineole is an oxabicycloalkane consisting of p-menthane with an epoxy bridge across positions 1 and 4. It has a role as a plant metabolite, a fumigant insecticide and a central nervous system depressant. It is a cineole and an oxabicycloalkane.

Name: 1,8-Cineole (Eucalyptol)
Desc: Eucalyptol is naturally produced cyclic ether and monoterpenoid. Eucalyptol is an ingredient in many brands of mouthwash and cough suppressant. It controls airway mucus hypersecretion and asthma via anti-inflammatory cytokine inhibition. Eucalyptol is an effective treatment for nonpurulent rhinosinusitis. Eucalyptol reduces inflammation and pain when applied topically. It kills leukaemia cells in vitro.

Name: 2-Methyl Benzothiophene
Desc: Colorless to pale yellow clear phenolic solvent that can be synthesized by reacting 2-thianaphthenyllithium with methyl p-toluenesulfonate.

Name: 2-Methyl Tetrahydrofuran (2-Me-THF)
Desc: Methyltetrahydrofuran appears as a colorless liquid with an ether-like odor. Less dense than water. Vapors heavier than air. Used to make other chemicals and as a solvent.

Name: 2-Methylnaphthalene
Desc: 2-methylnaphthalene is a white crystalline solid.

Name: 2-phenylbutene-1
Desc: 1-Phenyl-2-butene is a natural product found in Origanum sipyleum and Thymus longicaulis

Name: 2-Propanol
Desc: Isopropyl Alcohol is an isomer of propyl alcohol with antibacterial properties. Although the exact mechanism of isopropanol's disinfecting action is not known, it might kill cells by denaturing cell proteins and DNA, interfering with cellular metabolism, and dissolving cell lipo-protein membranes. Isopropanol is used in soaps and lotions as an antiseptic.

Name: 2,2-Dimethyltetrahydrofuran
Desc: 2,2-Dimethyltetrahydrofuran is a heterocyclic ether used in the synthesis of tetrahydrofuran and other tetrahydropyran derivatives

Name: 2,5-Dimethylthiophenol
Desc: 2,5-Dimethylbenzenethiol was used in the synthesis of poly(2-dodecanoylsulfanyl-p-phenylenevinylene).

Name: a-methylstyrene
Desc: Isopropenylbenzene appears as a colorless liquid. Insoluble in water and less dense than water. Flash point 115°F. May be mildly toxic by ingestion, inhalation and skin absorption. Vapors may be narcotic by inhalation. Used as a solvent and to make other chemicals.

Name: Acetone
Desc: Acetone is a manufactured chemical that is also found naturally in the environment. It is a colorless liquid with a distinct smell and taste. It evaporates easily, is flammable, and dissolves in water. It is also called dimethyl ketone, 2-propanone, and beta-ketopropane. Acetone is used to make plastic, fibers, drugs, and other chemicals. It is also used to dissolve other substances. It occurs naturally in plants, trees, volcanic gases, forest fires, and as a product of the breakdown of body fat. It is present in vehicle exhaust, tobacco smoke, and landfill sites. Industrial processes contribute more acetone to the environment than natural processes.

Name: Allyl Methyl Sulfide
Desc: Allyl methyl sulfide is a natural product found in Allium chinense, Dactylanthus taylorii, and other organisms

Name: Amyl Methyl Disulfide
Desc: Allyl methyl disulfide is an organic disulfide having allyl and methyl as the two organic groups. It has a role as a plant metabolite and a volatile oil component.

Name: Amyl methyl Sulfide
Desc: Amyl methyl sulfide is a natural product found in Brassica napus

Name: Anisole
Desc: Anisole appears as a clear straw-colored liquid with an aromatic odor. Insoluble in water and the same density as water. Vapors heavier than air. Moderately toxic by ingestion. A skin irritant. Used to make perfumes, flavorings and as a solvent.

Name: Artemisia Ketone
Desc: Flavoring Agent with a herbal honey mint berry odour.

Name: Benzaldehyde
Desc: Benzaldehyde appears as a clear colorless to yellow liquid with a bitter almond odor. Flash point near 145°F. More denser than water and insoluble in water. Hence sinks in water. Vapors are heavier than air. The primary hazard is to the environment. Immediate steps should be taken to limit spread to the environment. Easily penetrates the soil to contaminate groundwater and nearby waterways. Used in flavoring and perfume making.

Name: Benzyl Benzoate
Desc: Benzyl benzoate is a benzoate ester obtained by the formal condensation of benzoic acid with benzyl alcohol. It has been isolated from the plant species of the genus Polyalthia. It has a role as a scabicide, an acaricide and a plant metabolite. It is a benzyl ester and a benzoate ester. It derives from a benzoic acid.

Name: Bisabolene
Desc: (S)-beta-bisabolene is a beta-bisabolene which has (1S)-configuration. It is an enantiomer of a (R)-beta-bisabolene.

Name: Butyl Benzoate
Desc: Butyl benzoate is a benzoate ester obtained by condensation of benzoic acid and butanol. It is used as a perfume ingredient and as a solvent for cellulose ether, a dye carrier for textiles. It has a role as an antimicrobial food preservative, a fragrance and a plant metabolite.

Name: Carbon Disulfide (0 Dipole Moment)
Desc: Carbon disulfide appears as a clear colorless to light yellow volatile liquid with a strong disagreeable odor. Boiling point 46° C. Flash point -22°F. Flammable over a wide vapor/air concentration range(1%-50%). Vapors are readily ignited; the heat of a common light bulb may suffice. Insoluble in water and more dense (10.5 lb / gal) than water. Hence sinks in water. Vapors are heavier than air. Used in the manufacture of rayon and cellophane, in the manufacture of flotation agents and as a solvent.

Name: Carvone
Desc: Carvone is a p-menthane monoterpenoid that consists of cyclohex-2-enone having methyl and isopropenyl substituents at positions 2 and 5, respectively. It has a role as an allergen. It is a member of carvones and a botanical anti-fungal agent.

Name: Chlorobenzene
Desc: Chlorobenzene is a colorless, flammable liquid with an aromatic, almond-like odor. Some of it will dissolve in water, but it readily evaporates into air. It does not occur naturally in the environment. Chlorobenzene production in the United States has declined by more than 60% from its peak in 1960. It was used in the past to make other chemicals, such as phenol and DDT. Now chlorobenzene is used as a solvent for some pesticide formulations, to degrease automobile parts, and as a chemical intermediate to make several other chemicals.

Name: Chloroform
Desc: Most commonly used solvent for organic electronics fabrication

Name: Citral
Desc: Citral appears as a clear yellow colored liquid with a lemon-like odor. Less dense than water and insoluble in water. Toxic by ingestion. Used to make other chemicals.

Name: Citronellal
Desc: Citronellal is a monoterpenoid, the main component of citronella oil which gives it its distinctive lemon aroma. It has a role as a metabolite and an antifungal agent. It is a monoterpenoid and an aldehyde.

Name: Citronellol
Desc: Citronellol is a monoterpenoid that is oct-6-ene substituted by a hydroxy group at position 1 and methyl groups at positions 3 and 7. It has a role as a plant metabolite.

Name: Cocoa Butenal
Desc: 2-Phenyl-2-butenal is an olefinic compound.

Name: Cynamaldehyde
Desc: Cinnamaldehyde is a yellow oily liquid with a cinnamon odor and sweet taste.

Name: d-Limonene
Desc: A naturally-occurring class of moterpenes which occur as a clear colorless liquid at room temperature. Limonene is the major component in the oil of oranges which has many uses, including as flavor and fragrance. It is recognized as safe in food by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA).

Name: Dicyclohexyl disulfide
Desc: Dicyclohexyl disulfide is an organic disulfide.

Name: Diethyl Carbonate
Desc: Diethyl carbonate appears as a colorless liquid with a mild pleasant odor. It is slightly less dense than water and insoluble in water. Hence floats on water. Flash point 77°F. Vapors are heavier than air. When heated to high temperatures it may emit acrid smoke. Used as a solvent.

Name: Diethyl sulfide
Desc: Diethyl sulfide appears as a colorless oily liquid with a garlic-like odor. Less dense than water. Vapors heavier than air. May irritate skin and eyes. Used to make other chemicals.

Name: Diethylene Glycol
Desc: Diethylene glycol appears as a colorless liquid. Denser than water. Contact may slightly irritate skin, eyes and mucous membranes. May be slightly toxic by ingestion. Used to make other chemicals.

Name: Dimethyl Disulfide
Desc: Dimethyl disulfide appears as a colorless oily liquid with a garlic-like odor. Denser than water and slightly soluble in water. Vapors heavier than air. May irritate skin and eyes. Used to make other chemicals.

Name: Dimethyl Sulfide
Desc: Dimethyl sulfide appears as a clear colorless to straw colored liquid with a disagreeable odor. Flash point less than 0°F. Less dense than water and slightly soluble in water. Vapors are heavier than air.

Name: Dimethyl Sulfoxide (DMSO)
Desc: Dimethyl Sulfoxide is a highly polar organic liquid that is used widely as a chemical solvent and a free radical scavenger. It shows a range of pharmacological activity including analgesia and anti-inflammation. Because of its ability to penetrate biological membranes, it is used as a vehicle for topical application of pharmaceuticals. It is also used to protect cells and tissue during cryopreservation and has been used to treat extravasation damage caused by anthracycline-based chemotherapy.

Name: Dipentene
Desc: Limonene is a monoterpene that is cyclohex-1-ene substituted by a methyl group at position 1 and a prop-1-en-2-yl group at position 4 respectively. It has a role as a human metabolite. It is a monoterpene and a cycloalkene. It derives from a hydride of a p-menthane.

Name: Diphenyl Ether
Desc: Diphenyl ether is an aromatic ether in which the oxygen is attached to two phenyl substituents. It has been found in muscat grapes and vanilla. It has a role as a plant metabolite.

Name: Diphenyl sulfide
Desc: Diphenyl sulfide is an aryl sulfide that consists of two phenyl groups connected by a sulphur atom.

Name: Diphenylmethane
Desc: Diphenylmethane is a diarylmethane that is methane substituted by two phenyl groups.

Name: Dipropyl Disulfide
Desc: Dipropyl disulfide is an organic disulfide where the alkyl groups specified are propyl. It is a component of the essential oils obtained from Allium. It has a role as a plant metabolite.

Name: Ethanol
Desc: Ethanol is a primary alcohol that is ethane in which one of the hydrogens is substituted by a hydroxy group. It has a role as an antiseptic drug, a polar solvent, a neurotoxin, a central nervous system depressant, a teratogenic agent, a NMDA receptor antagonist, a protein kinase C agonist, a disinfectant, a human metabolite, a Saccharomyces cerevisiae metabolite, an Escherichia coli metabolite and a mouse metabolite. It is a primary alcohol, an alkyl alcohol, a volatile organic compound and a member of ethanols. It is a conjugate acid of an ethoxide.

Name: Ethanolamine
Desc: Monoethanolamine is a first generation monoethanolamine with antihistaminic property. Ethanolamine competes with free histamine for binding at the histamine (H)-1 receptor thereby acting as an inverse agonist that combines with and stabilizes the inactive form of the H1-receptor thereby shifting the equilibrium toward the inactive state. This leads to a reduction of the negative symptoms brought on by H1-receptor binding.

Name: Ethyl Acetate
Desc: Ethyl acetate appears as a clear colorless liquid with a fruity odor. Flash point 24°F. Less dense than water. Vapors heavier than air.

Name: Ethylene Glycol
Desc: Ethylene glycol is a clear, sweet, slightly viscous liquid that boils at 198 °C (388.4 °F). Its most common use is as an automotive antifreeze.

Name: Ethylene Glycol Monomethyl Ether
Desc: Also known as 2-Methoxyethanol,  it is used as a solvent for many different purposes, (e.g., varnishes, dyes, and resins) and as a jet deicing additive.

Name: Eucalyptol
Desc: a liquid C10H18O with an odor of camphor that occurs in many essential oils (as of eucalyptus) and is used especially as an expectorant and flavoring agent. — called also cineole.

Name: Eucarvone
Desc: Eucarvone is a natural terpene found in Teucrium polium, Asarum hypogynum,  black currant, angelica root, and other organisms.

Name: Farnesol
Desc: Farnesol is a colorless liquid with a delicate floral odor  found in Lonicera japonica, Alpinia hainanensis, and other organisms

Name: Geraniol
Desc: Geraniol is a monoterpene that is found within many essential oils of fruits, vegetables, and herbs including rose oil, citronella, lemongrass, lavender, and other aromatic plants. It is emitted from the flowers of many species of plant and is commonly used by the food, fragrance, and cosmetic industry

Name: Glycerol
Desc: Used as a solvent, humectant, plasticizer, emollient, sweetener, coating for paper, antifreeze for automobiles, and fluid for gas meters, hydraulic jacks, and shock absorber; Also used to make nitroglycerol (dynamite), cosmetics, soaps, liqueurs, confectioneries, inks, lubricants, glues; and medications; Also used to keep fabrics pliable; to preserve printing on cotton; and to defrost windshields

Name: Heptane
Desc: Heptane is the straight-chain alkane with the chemical formula H3C(CH2)5CH3 or C7H16, and is one of the main components of gasoline (petrol)

Name: Indane
Desc: Indane is an ortho-fused bicyclic hydrocarbon consisting of a benzene ring fused to a cyclopentane ring; a high-boiling (176 (o)C) colourless liquid. It is a member of indanes and an ortho-fused bicyclic hydrocarbon.

Name: Isobutylamine
Desc: Isobutylamine is an organic chemical compound (specifically, an amine) with the formula (CH3)2CHCH2NH2, and occurs as a colorless liquid. Isobutylamine is one of the four isomeric amines of butane, the others being n-butylamine, sec-butylamine and tert-butylamine.

Name: Jasminone
Desc: Also known as 2-(trans-2-Pentenyl)cyclopentanone, it is a cyclic ketone. with Lactonic, peach, creamy coconut with apricot and coumarin undertones. Smooth and creamy notes to enrich floral, fruity, and tropical types for personal care and fine fragrances.

Name: L-Menthone
Desc: Menthone is a monoterpene with a minty flavor that occurs naturally in a number of essential oils. Menthone is a natural product found in Xylopia aromatica, Hedeoma multiflora, and other organisms

Name: Laevo-Fenchone
Desc: L-fenchone is a constituent of the essential oils obtained from fennel. It has a role as a plant metabolite. It has camphor herbal earthy woody scent

Name: Laevo-Rose-Oxide
Desc: Rose oxide is a fragrance chemical found in roses and rose oil. It also contributes to the flavor of some fruits, such as lychee, and wines, such as Gewürztraminer.

Name: Leaf Acetal
Desc: Leaf acetal has been found in Guava and Plum. It  is used as natural green top notes in floral fragrances insluding shampoos, soaps and detergents as well as in mossy or citrus perfumes and fruity flavors with reminiscence of tropical fruits.

Name: Linalool
Desc: Linalool occurs both free and in the form of esters in many essential oils and is used in perfumes, soaps, and flavoring materials as it has a spicy herbal odor.

Name: Linalyl acetate
Desc: Linalyl acetate is a naturally occurring phytochemical found in many flowers and spice plants. It is one of the principal components of the essential oils of bergamot and lavender. Chemically, it is the acetate ester of linalool, and the two often occur in conjunction.

Name: m-Methylstyrene
Desc: 3-Methylstyreneis used as pharmaceutical intermediate

Name: m-Xylene
Desc: It is one of the three isomers of dimethylbenzene known collectively as xylenes. The m- stands for meta-, indicating that the two methyl groups in m-xylene occupy positions 1 and 3 on a benzene ring.

Name: Mesitylene
Desc: Mesitylene is a colorless liquid with sweet aromatic odor. It is a component of coal tar, which is its traditional source. It  is natural product found in Lepidium meyenii and Ferulago nodosa

Name: Methanol
Desc: Methanol is a toxic alcohol that is used industrially as a solvent, pesticide, and alternative fuel source. It also occurs naturally in humans, animals, and plants.

Name: o-Methylanisole
Desc: 2-methylanisole is a monomethoxybenzene that is o-cresol in which phenolic hydroxy group has been converted to the corresponding methyl ether. A 'green' solvent (b.p. 171 ℃) and food flavour ingredient, it is found in mastic oils, virgin olive oils and frankincense.

Name: O-Xylene
Desc: O-xylene appears as a colorless watery liquid with a sweet odor. It is the most commonly used 'green solvent' for OPV.

Name: Perillaldehyde
Desc: Perillaldehyde is a natural organic compound found most abundantly in the annual herb perilla, but also in a wide variety of other plants and essential oils. It is used as food additives for flavoring and in perfumery to add spiciness

Name: Phellandrene
Desc: It has a role as a volatile oil component, a plant metabolite and an antimicrobial agent.

Name: Water
Desc: The ideal green solvent.
